# Cipi

> Cipi is a Laravel-first open-source deploy CLI that also supports static sites and generic PHP apps. One command installs a complete production stack (Nginx, PHP, MariaDB, Valkey; optional PostgreSQL) on any Ubuntu VPS. It is CLI-first, with an optional self-hosted web control panel (GUI) you can install if you want a browser dashboard. MIT licensed, self-hosted alternative to Laravel Forge.

Full plain-text site content for LLM ingestion: https://cipi.sh/llms-full.txt

## Site

English only. Public URLs have no language prefix: homepage `https://cipi.sh/`, docs `https://cipi.sh/docs/`, and so on. `/en/…` 301s to the same path without `/en`. Former language trees (`/de`, `/fr`, `/it`, `/es`, `/pt`) and localized slugs 301 to the English equivalent. There is no Accept-Language or cookie redirect.

Key facts:

- Install: `wget -O - https://cipi.sh/setup.sh | bash`
- Admin access: SSH as `cipi` user, then `sudo -s` to run `cipi` commands
- Optional web GUI: `cipi gui <domain>` installs an opt-in Laravel control panel to manage one or more servers from the browser; Cipi stays fully usable CLI-only without it. GUI supports .env / auth.json / Artisan / App commands (API 1.14+ / Cipi 5.0.3+), server cockpit — PHP, SSH, services, SMTP, health, IP whitelist (API 1.15+ / Cipi 5.0.6+), Octane create (API 1.13+ / Cipi 5.0+), and multi-engine MariaDB/PostgreSQL (API 1.12+ / Cipi 4.8+)
- Current release: Cipi **5.3.0**, panel API **1.20**. 5.3.0 adds **Cloudflare Zero Trust** (`cipi zt`, opt-in — `setup.sh` and `cipi self-update` never install `cloudflared` or call `enable`): `cipi zt token set --token= --account=` (root-only `/etc/cipi/zt.token`; needs Account.Cloudflare Tunnel Edit, Account.Access: Apps and Policies Edit, Zone.DNS Edit, plus Zone.SSL and Certificates Edit for Origin CA; not `/etc/cipi/cloudflare.ini`, which stays certbot DNS-01); `enable` (official cloudflared package, locally-managed tunnel, systemd unit, nginx `real_ip` from `api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/ips` reading `CF-Connecting-IP`, fail2ban `ignoreip` backup of the ranges, CrowdSec allowlist when CrowdSec is on, daily `cipi zt refresh` cron; does **not** close 22/80/443); `hostname add <app|--gui>` (CNAME to `{tunnel-id}.cfargotunnel.com`, ingress `http://127.0.0.1:80`, public CDN/WAF, no Access; `cipi app create` does not add it, `cipi zt status` lists apps not on the tunnel); `access enable <app|--gui>` (Cloudflare Access, any authenticated user; a Bypass application for `/cipi/webhook` when the app has a Git webhook); `ssh enable --hostname=` (ingress `ssh://127.0.0.1:22` + Access SSH app, prints the `ProxyCommand cloudflared access ssh` config; port 22 stays open; Deployer still SSHs to localhost); `lock http [--yes]` (refuses while any app renews Let's Encrypt over HTTP-01, `--force` skips; closes 80/443 if every HTTP hostname is on the tunnel, else allows 80/443 only from Cloudflare ranges); `lock ssh [--yes]` (only if cloudflared is active and the tunnel has SSH ingress; rescue `cipi zt ssh unlock`); `origin-cert <app>` (optional 15-year Cloudflare Origin CA; marks the app so `cipi ssl install` HTTP-01 will not overwrite it); `status|disable|refresh|unlock http`; `disable` restores UFW 22/80/443, removes cloudflared and the tunnel, leaves Let's Encrypt alone. `cipi ssl install` HTTP-01 refuses under `lock http` and on Origin CA apps; tunneled apps get certbot `--no-redirect`; `cipi ssl force` refuses on them. Triggers `zt_enable`, `zt_disable`, `zt_lock_http`, `zt_lock_ssh`. 5.3.0 also adds **`cipi monitor`** — server checks every 5 minutes from `/etc/cron.d/cipi-monitor` (`/usr/local/bin/cipi-monitor`), state files in `/var/log/cipi/monitor/`, no metrics storage: `disk` (warn ≥80% / crit ≥90%), `ssl` (Let's Encrypt expiry ≤14 days), `services` (every installed Cipi service via systemd), `workers` (`*-worker-*` / `*-horizon` must be RUNNING), `http_5xx` (≥20 and ≥5% of requests in the bytes appended since the previous run; per-log offsets survive logrotate; first run only baselines), `fs` (`/etc/cipi` or `/var/log/cipi` read-only), `load` (>4× cores for 2 consecutive runs); edge-triggered (ok→fail once, warn↔crit once, recovery `monitor_ok`, reminder every `reminder_minutes`, default 240); `cipi monitor [--json]` exits 1 on warn/crit, `list`, `enable|disable <check>`, `set disk --warn= --crit=`, `set ssl --days=`, `set http_5xx --count= --ratio=`, `set load --factor= --runs=`, `set reminder --minutes=`, `test`; triggers `monitor_disk|ssl|services|workers|http_5xx|fs|load|ok`. And **alert channels**: `cipi notifications channel add <slack|discord|ntfy|telegram|webhook> <id> --url=` (Telegram `--token= --chat-id=`; ntfy `--priority=`), `list|remove|enable|disable|test <id|all>`, stored encrypted in `/etc/cipi/alerts.json`; every existing trigger fans out to chat as well as email (no SMTP needed for chat); 5-second timeout per channel, failures only logged to `events.log`; ntfy urgent triggers raised to high priority; Discord truncated at 2000 chars, Telegram at 4096; webhook JSON `{server, trigger, subject, body, ts}`; no channel = email-only as before. **Fixed in 5.3.0:** jq `// true` read an explicit `false` as true — `cipi notifications disable <trigger>` kept firing, `cipi smtp configure --tls=off` was ignored (msmtp always got `tls on`), and `health: {enabled: false}` in `cipi.yml` did nothing; now `!= false` / `has()`. Migration 5.3.0 installs the monitor cron and default `monitor.json` / `alerts.json`, regenerates panel API sudoers (`zt status`, `monitor list`; enable/lock/set stay CLI-only) and refreshes completion; it configures no channel and enables no Zero Trust. 5.2.3 extends `cipi git` beyond GitHub/GitLab: **Cursor Origin** (`origin.cursor.com`), **AWS CodeCommit** (`git-codecommit.*.amazonaws.com`), **Bitbucket Cloud** (`bitbucket.org`) and **Azure DevOps** (`dev.azure.com` / `ssh.dev.azure.com` / `*.visualstudio.com`) are detected from the SSH clone URL; `cipi git origin-token|bitbucket-token|azure-token|codecommit-token <access-key> <secret-key> <iam-user>` plus matching `remove-*`; deploy key always registered, webhook where the forge has one (Bitbucket `repo:push` + HMAC `secret`; Azure `git.push` service hook sending `X-Gitlab-Token`); Origin and CodeCommit have no per-repo HTTP webhook, so deploy with `cipi deploy`. CodeCommit uses IAM `UploadSSHPublicKey` via curl `--aws-sigv4`, mints a 4096-bit `id_rsa` (IAM refuses ed25519) and writes `~/.ssh/config` so the SSH Key ID is the username; IAM allows five SSH keys per user. New apps keyscan `bitbucket.org`, `origin.cursor.com`, `ssh.dev.azure.com` and the repository URL host. CrowdSec allowlists Bitbucket egress CIDRs from `ip-ranges.atlassian.com` (fail-open); Azure/Origin need `cipi crowdsec allow` if banned. 5.2.3 also adds **`deploy.post` in `cipi.yml`** — allowlisted post-deploy steps (`artisan`, `npm`/`npx`/`yarn`/`pnpm`, `composer`, one relative `php`/`node` script), no free shell, run on both `cipi deploy` and the webhook and **without** `cipi yml auto`; `deploy.post_on_failure: warn` (default, mails `yml_post_fail`) or `abort`; `cipi yml post-deploy <app>` runs them now. And **manual stack upgrades**: `cipi nginx upgrade`, `cipi db upgrade [mariadb|pgsql]`, `cipi service upgrade [nginx|mariadb|postgresql|valkey]` — patch-level only, `--yes` to skip the prompt, `all` refused, never on a cron, not granted by `/etc/sudoers.d/cipi-api`; shared `lib/stack-upgrade.sh`, lock `/run/cipi-stack-upgrade.lock`, mails `nginx_upgrade`/`mariadb_upgrade`/`pgsql_upgrade`/`valkey_upgrade`. **Security fix in 5.2.3:** a custom app serves `htdocs/` as document root, so a committed `cipi.yml` answered at `https://domain/cipi.yml`; every app vhost now denies `/cipi.yml` and `/cipi.yaml` at any path (Laravel included), applied on update without regenerating the vhost, and `cipi yml` also looks in `htdocs/`. 5.2.2 adds two more opt-in commands, neither installed by `setup.sh` or `cipi self-update`: **`cipi search`** (Meilisearch as a native binary for Laravel Scout — 127.0.0.1 only, Cipi-written `SCOUT_PREFIX`, app delete revokes the key, clone mints a new one) and **`cipi package`** (allowlisted apt for host binaries: image-optimizers, ffmpeg, imagemagick, poppler-utils; Chromium is refused because it would pull snapd). 5.2.0 adds **opt-in CrowdSec** and a **nightly integrity scan** — neither is installed by `setup.sh` or `cipi self-update`, and there is no WAF. `cipi crowdsec enable` installs the engine **and** a registered firewall bouncer (`crowdsec-firewall-bouncer-nftables|-iptables` via `cscli bouncers add`), reads `/home/*/logs/nginx-{access,error}.log`, refuses below 512MB MemAvailable or behind a reverse proxy without `set_real_ip_from`/`real_ip_header` (`--force` overrides), allowlists the current SSH session, and starts a rescue TLS listener whose one-shot token allowlists the TCP peer and unbans it in CrowdSec and fail2ban (`cipi crowdsec rescue token|rotate`, `allow|unallow`). `disable` flushes the CrowdSec chains before purging. Allowlists cover localhost, RFC1918, Let's Encrypt, GitHub webhook CIDRs from `api.github.com/meta` `.hooks` (fail-open) and hardcoded GitLab.com CIDRs dated 2026-09-07. `cipi ban list|unban` includes CrowdSec when the engine is up. `cipi scan` runs nightly at 04:40: sha256 integrity of `current/` (or `htdocs/`) against a manifest written at every deploy and rollback in `/var/lib/cipi/manifests` (root:root 0600), then one ClamAV pass over upload dirs only with rfxn PHP-webshell signatures; mails `scan_integrity` or `scan_incomplete` — never a false "clean". `enable` refuses below 2GB MemAvailable or 3GB free on `/var`. Bash and zsh tab-completion is installed automatically by `setup.sh` and every `self-update` (`cipi completion bash|zsh [--print]`). Migration 5.2.0 installs `cipi-scan-manifest` and the rescue helpers, creates the manifest store, grants per-app manifest sudo entries, and adds `SSH_CLIENT`/`SSH_CONNECTION` to `env_keep` in `/etc/sudoers.d/cipi-sudo` (validated with `visudo -c`); it enables nothing. 5.2.1 added `cipi git refresh` and `cipi app fix-permissions`. 5.1.3 fixed `cipi ini list`; 5.1.2 made Laravel Reverb production-ready (generated credentials, `ws://`/`wss://` from the certificate, a proxy matching only `/app/{key}` and `/apps/{id}/…`, `workers.reverb` in `cipi.yml`); 5.1.1 repaired FPM pools and wildcard domains end to end
- Stack: Nginx, PHP 8.x, MariaDB (default), optional PostgreSQL, Valkey, Supervisor; optional Laravel Octane (FrankenPHP) beside FPM (v5.0+)
- Databases (v4.8.0+): MariaDB on 3306 + optional PostgreSQL on 5432; `cipi db install|uninstall|default|engines`; `--engine=mariadb|pgsql` on db/app commands
- www redirects (v4.8.0+): `cipi www add|force-to-root|force-from-root|clear|status`; `cipi ssl force` re-applies HTTPS redirect
- Backup profiles (v5.1.0+): `cipi backup profile add` — scope (all/files/db), schedule, dest (local/s3), retention, `--encrypt`; databases discovered from the engine (tenant DBs included); `cipi backup verify|status|fetch`; managed crontab block
- `cipi.yml` (v5.1.0+): optional per-project file for aliases, PHP, extra DBs, workers (Horizon; Reverb since 5.1.2), healthcheck, backups, and post-deploy steps (`deploy.post`, since 5.2.3); `cipi yml generate|plan|apply|auto|post-deploy`; looked up in `current/`, `shared/` and `htdocs/` (5.2.3), and never served over HTTP (5.2.3)
- `cipi ini` (v5.1.0+): guided php.ini for FPM and CLI, server-wide or `--app=`; whitelist of settable keys
- Post-deploy healthchecks (v5.1.0+): verify the live release after every deploy; optional `--rollback-on-unhealthy` (does not undo migrations)
- Nginx default-server (v5.1.0+): unmatched Host on :80/:443 closed with 444; wildcard aliases (`cipi alias add '*.example.com'`)
- CrowdSec (v5.2.0+, opt-in): `cipi crowdsec enable|disable|status|allow|unallow|rescue`; engine plus a registered firewall bouncer; rescue TLS listener with a one-shot break-glass token; not a WAF
- Integrity + malware scan (v5.2.0+, opt-in): `cipi scan enable|disable|status|report|manifest|<app>`; nightly 04:40; sha256 vs the deploy manifest, then ClamAV on upload dirs only
- Shell completion (v5.2.0+): bash and zsh completion installed by `setup.sh` and every `self-update`; `cipi completion bash|zsh [--print]` for non-login shells
- Search (v5.2.2+, opt-in): `cipi search install|enable|disable|list|status|key|upgrade|remove` — native Meilisearch for Laravel Scout; 127.0.0.1 only; Cipi writes `SCOUT_PREFIX`; not in `cipi backup`
- Host packages (v5.2.2+, opt-in): `cipi package list|install|remove` — allowlisted Ubuntu binaries (image-optimizers, ffmpeg, imagemagick, poppler-utils); Chromium refused
- Git forges (v5.2.3+): auto-setup for GitHub, GitLab, Cursor Origin, AWS CodeCommit, Bitbucket Cloud and Azure DevOps; `cipi git status|refresh|<provider>-token|remove-<provider>`
- Manual stack upgrades (v5.2.3+): `cipi nginx upgrade`, `cipi db upgrade [engine]`, `cipi service upgrade [nginx|mariadb|postgresql|valkey]` — patch-level, operator-triggered, never scheduled; the four packages kept off unattended-upgrades
- Cloudflare Zero Trust (v5.3.0+, opt-in): `cipi zt token|enable|disable|status|refresh|hostname|access|ssh|lock|unlock|origin-cert` — locally-managed tunnel, nginx real_ip, Cloudflare Access for staging/GUI/SSH, `lock http` / `lock ssh` to close the origin (both refuse when unsafe); fail2ban and UFW stay
- System monitor (v5.3.0+, on by default): `cipi monitor [--json]|list|enable|disable|set|test` — disk, SSL expiry, services, workers, 5xx spikes, read-only fs, load every 5 minutes; alerts on state change, recovery and a reminder every 4h
- Alert channels (v5.3.0+): `cipi notifications channel add|list|test|enable|disable|remove` — Slack, Discord, Telegram, ntfy, JSON webhook for every notification trigger; best-effort, 5s timeout
- Panel API (`cipi/api` 1.20): REST + 50+ MCP tools; app `.env` / `auth.json` / Artisan / app-run / deploy-config (Cipi 5.0.3+); server cockpit — PHP install/default, SSH keys, services, SMTP, healthchecks, IP whitelist (Cipi 5.0.6+ / API 1.15+); `POST /api/apps` accepts `octane` and `engine`; list/show expose `octane`/`octane_port`; www + multi-engine DB endpoints (1.12+)
- PHP security patches: managed by Cipi (`cipi php upgrade`), not unattended-upgrades; weekly check Sunday 03:30 (v4.7.13+)
- nginx / MariaDB / PostgreSQL / Valkey patches: also off unattended-upgrades, but manual only — `cipi nginx upgrade`, `cipi db upgrade`, `cipi service upgrade` (v5.2.3+)
- S3 backups: staging dir defaults to /var/tmp, not /tmp (v4.7.14+); override via backup.json tmpdir or CIPI_BACKUP_TMPDIR
- SMTP: send via system `/etc/msmtprc` only (AppArmor/setgid-safe); legacy `/etc/cipi/.msmtprc` removed (v4.7.22 / migrations 4.7.20–4.7.22)
- Deploy SSH: `~/.ssh` must be mode 700 (not group-writable); `cipi app create` enforces it; `cipi app delete` purges orphan users/homes (v4.7.19)
- Panel API on Ubuntu 25.10+/26.04: sudo-rs sudoers, read-only /etc/cipi guards, open_basedir for log helpers, empty DBs in `cipi db list` (v4.7.18 / migrations 4.7.15–4.7.18)
- Integrations: GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket Cloud, Azure DevOps (auto webhook + deploy keys), Cursor Origin and AWS CodeCommit (deploy key only), custom Git via SSH, webhooks, MCP server for AI agents, native alert channels — Slack, Discord, Telegram, ntfy, webhook (v5.3.0+) — plus CI deploy-notification examples

## Docs

- [Documentation Index](https://cipi.sh/docs/): Full technical documentation hub
- [Getting Started](https://cipi.sh/docs/getting-started): Installation, requirements, quick start, tech stack, app structure
- [Cipi Agent](https://cipi.sh/docs/agent): Laravel package `cipi/agent` — webhooks, health check, in-app MCP, database anonymizer ([GitHub](https://github.com/cipi-sh/agent))
- [Apps](https://cipi.sh/docs/apps): Create, manage, and configure Laravel and custom applications
- [Deploy & CI/CD](https://cipi.sh/docs/deploy): Zero-downtime deployments, Git integration, CI/CD pipelines, notifications
- [Infrastructure](https://cipi.sh/docs/infrastructure): PHP, databases, SSL, backups, workers, firewall, CrowdSec, Cloudflare Zero Trust, system monitor, Meilisearch, host packages, server management
- [CLI Client](https://cipi.sh/docs/cli-client): Remote `cipi-cli` — manage servers from the terminal via the REST API
- [Control Panel (GUI)](https://cipi.sh/docs/gui): Optional self-hosted web control panel — apps (incl. Octane / engine), databases, SSL, www, deploys, 2FA/TOTP, multi-server ([GitHub](https://github.com/cipi-sh/gui))
- [Advanced](https://cipi.sh/docs/advanced): REST API (1.20), server sync, vault encryption, SMTP and chat alert channels, IP whitelist, log retention, advanced config
- [About Cipi](https://cipi.sh/docs/about): History, security model, design decisions, comparisons
- [cipi.yml](https://cipi.sh/cipi-yml): The per-app configuration file committed with the code — aliases, PHP and php.ini, extra databases, queue workers or Horizon, Laravel Reverb (5.1.2+), scheduler, healthcheck and backup profiles, reconciled with `cipi yml plan` / `cipi yml apply`

## API & CLI

- [Installation & Quick Start](https://cipi.sh/docs/getting-started#installation): Server requirements, setup script, post-install access
- [Cipi API](https://cipi.sh/docs/advanced#cipi-api): Server REST API + MCP + Swagger — current package **1.20** (`cipi/api`, [release 1.20](https://github.com/cipi-sh/api/releases/tag/1.20), [GitHub](https://github.com/cipi-sh/api))
- [CLI Client](https://cipi.sh/docs/cli-client): Remote terminal client for apps, databases, SSL, deploys
- [WHMCS Module](https://cipi.sh/docs/advanced#whmcs): WHMCS provisioning module for billing automation
- [Agent — MCP Server](https://cipi.sh/docs/agent#agent-mcp): Model Context Protocol server for AI agents

- [Manage Laravel apps with cipi.yml](https://cipi.sh/guides/manage-apps-with-cipi-yml): Generate, plan and apply aliases, PHP, workers, Reverb, healthchecks and backups from a committed `cipi.yml`, then opt in so every deploy reconciles

- [Kamal Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-kamal): Full server panel alternative to Kamal — native LEMP, not just Docker deploys
- [RunCloud Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-runcloud): Laravel-native, free alternative to RunCloud

- [Coolify Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-coolify): Laravel-native, CLI-first alternative to Coolify for teams that prefer a native LEMP stack over Docker
- [Dokku Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-dokku): Laravel-first alternative to Dokku with full server provisioning
- [Easypanel Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-easypanel): Laravel-native alternative to Easypanel without Docker overhead
- [Vito Deploy Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-vito-deploy): CLI-first, single-binary alternative to Vito Deploy
- [cPanel Alternative](https://cipi.sh/alternative-to-cpanel): Lightweight, Laravel-native alternative to cPanel
